methodology.constructive_sample_rule: For each surviving quartet, choose the earliest source_id for each signature class 0..15 in sorted source_id order.
methodology.equivalence_rules: Exact dataset duplicates, complement equivalence, and full-dataset implication constraints are tracked separately; implication is a validity constraint, not feature collapse.
methodology.feature_selection: Eligibility from feature_registry.csv where eligible_for_gameplay is true and constant features are excluded.
methodology.global_feasibility_condition: For each quartet, evaluate every element in the eligible population, form the 4-bit signature, and require all 16 possible signature classes to appear at least once.

qualitative_factors: Only 203 of 3060 candidate quartets are globally feasible under all-16-signature coverage.
The feasible subset is therefore a minority of the eligible feature space (203 / 3060 = 0.0663).
A valid sample requires one selected entity for each of 16 signature classes, making it much more restrictive than a single globally feasible quartet count alone.
The failure of 1024 random samples is consistent with a combination of global scarcity and sparse class coverage, not a single defect in the implementation.
